recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Government for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: C. C. Dibie
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Meaning, Nature and Scope of Government
subtopics: Government as an institution of the state, as a process, and as an academic field of study
Characteristics of the state: Population, territory, government, sovereignty
Functions of government: Law making, defense, maintenance of law and order, provision of social amenities
objectives: Define government in its three distinct dimensions
Distinguish a state from a government or nation
Explain 5 reasons why government is indispensable in society

topics.topic: Basic Political Concepts: Power, Authority and Legitimacy
subtopics: Meaning and forms of power (military, economic, political)
Sources of authority: Traditional, charismatic, rational-legal (Max Weber)
Legitimacy: Factors that confer and factors that undermine government legitimacy
objectives: Differentiate naked power from legitimate authority
Classify historical African leaders into Weber's authority typologies
Explain how corruption and rigged elections destroy governmental legitimacy

topics.topic: Sovereignty, Rule of Law and Constitutionalism
subtopics: Concept of sovereignty (Jean Bodin): Legal, political, de facto, and de jure sovereignty
Principles of the Rule of Law (A.V. Dicey): Supremacy of law, equality before the law, fundamental human rights
Constitutionalism and checks against executive tyranny
objectives: Define sovereignty and state 4 limitations on national sovereignty
Explain the 3 cardinal tenets of A.V. Dicey's Rule of Law
Analyze real-life obstacles to the rule of law in developing democracies

topics.topic: Organs of Government: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
subtopics: Legislature: Unicameral vs bicameral systems, functions, bill passage procedure
Executive: Presidential vs parliamentary executives, functions and powers
Judiciary: Hierarchy of courts, judicial independence, judicial review
objectives: Compare unicameral and bicameral legislative structures
Explain 5 mechanisms that safeguard the independence of the judiciary
Trace the life cycle of a legislative bill from first reading to presidential assent
